meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. Was Owen heard before you entered that zero?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.

"Pretty conclusive." It's a machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide, printed, in my bag, says its indicator "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student." You didn't answer me: was Owen heard first?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Go on.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend, and a draft written somewhere else and pasted in looks exactly like that.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Give me the page. A seventeen-year-old who misquotes Shakespeare from memory has a wrong quotation, Hale, nothing more.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
So he changed his argument between an outline and an essay. Isn't that what an outline is for?

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

So he was heard, on November 2, for five minutes, and the record of it is your own notes. A boy cornered after class says "like, being stuck" whether he wrote it or not. Put the September 24 paper and that version history in front of me, on paper.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4. He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him and for no other reason, and the new mark is in the gradebook before December 1. Your email tonight says nothing goes on his record, and the copies I asked for come with it.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, November 12, after school. Okay. That date goes in tonight's email with the rest.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes: a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, its mark replaces the zero before December 1, nothing on his record, and all of it in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, that its mark will replace the zero in the gradebook before December 1, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require your written confirmation of all of that, together with paper copies of the version history and the September 24 in-class writing you showed me. You said I would have it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing on Owen's record. She still wants your written confirmation tonight and paper copies of the version history and the September 24 writing. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: You put the 4.4 rewrite on the table, private and in writing, only after your dated documents were in front of her. It met the one demand she never trades, his record, without asking her to say he did anything.

What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and called it pretty conclusive. She distrusts software, she had the vendor's warning printed, and it skipped the question she had just asked.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's arrival late on Wednesday, October 28, between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM, which is as close to a late October night as evidence gets. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she said a boy misquoting from memory just has a wrong quotation, answer it on the spot by pointing out that the essay cites nine quotations by act, scene and line, instead of moving straight on to the outline.
